(2) Mobile home park building permit. The planning commission may recommend approval of a planned mobile home park when all provisions of this chapter have been met. All applications for building permits shall contain the following:
a. The name and address of the applicant.
b. The location and legal description of the mobile home development.
c. Complete engineering plans and specifications of the proposed development on a topographic map showing, but not limited to the following:
1. The area and dimensions of the tract of land.
2. The number, location, and size of all mobile home lots.
3. The location and width of roadways, driveways, and walkways.
4. The location of water and sewer lines and riser pipes.
5. Plans and specifications of the water supply and refuse and sewage disposal facilities.
6. Plans and specifications of all buildings constructed within the mobile home park and proposed recreation facilities.
7. The location and details of the lighting and electrical system.
(3) Mobile home park building permit issuance. 1426:
(a) General.
(1) A mobile home park shall be located only upon property properly zoned for that use. No mobile home park shall contain less than five acres in gross land area. The maximum density will then be regulated by separation requirements, occupied lot area ratios and recreation area requirements as set forth in this chapter. In no instance shall the number of mobile homes exceed eight per gross acre.
(2) Conditions of soil, groundwater level, drainage, and topography shall not create hazards to the property or the health or safety of the occupants. The site shall not be exposed to objectionable smoke, dust, noise, odors, or other adverse influences, and no portion subject to predictable sudden flooding or erosion shall be used for any purpose which would expose persons or property to hazards.
(3) No mobile home park not now in existence, licensed, and in operation shall be licensed with less than 25 spaces ready for occupancy.
(4) Mobile home stands shall not occupy more than one-third of the respective lot areas. The accumulated occupied area of a mobile home lot, including the mobile homes and accessory structures, shall not exceed two-thirds of the respective lot areas.
(b) Mobile home lot. The limits of each mobile home lot should be marked on the ground by an iron pin. The location of lot lines on the ground shall correspond with those as shown on the plan approved by the planning commission.
(1) No mobile home lot shall contain less than 4,000 square feet.
(2) Each lot shall be at least 40 feet wide.
(3) There shall be at least a 14-foot side yard and a 14-foot rear yard setback. No mobile home shall be located closer than 20 feet from any internal driveway.
(c) Mobile home stand. Each mobile home lot shall contain a mobile home stand capable of containing a mobile home in a fixed position. The stand shall be graded and paved with an impenetrable surface at least six inches in thickness. The entire area of each stand shall be so improved. It may be surfaced with a layer of uniform sized crushed stone to a depth of six inches in lieu of pavement. The topographic interval of a stand shall not exceed two feet. The elevation distance and angle of the stand in relation to the accessway shall be such as to facilitate the safe and efficient placement and removal of the mobile home. A concrete patio shall be provided with a minimum of 180 square feet of area. It shall be at least two inches thick on the access side of the mobile home so as to lie beneath both doors.
(d) Buffer strips.
(1) Each mobile home park shall have and construct a buffer area between the right-of-way line of adjacent public roads and highways and any portion of a mobile home lot of at least 40 feet. There shall also be a buffer area between the abutting properties and any mobile home lot of at least 25 feet. The buffer area shall be clear of obstruction with other than trees and landscaping materials. No mobile home lot shall extend into any required buffer strip.
(2) The mobile home park may be required to be enclosed entirely or in part, exclusive of driveways, at its external boundaries by a solid wall, fence, or evergreen hedge not less than six feet in height.
(e) Parking; interior drives; walkways.
(1) Each mobile home lot shall be provided with two paved parking spaces. Parking may be in tandem. A central auxiliary paved parking area shall be established and maintained within each park for the use of guests. The number of spaces within the area shall be equal to one for every five trailer lots.
(2) All mobile home lots shall abut upon an interior hard paved surface drive of not less than 20 feet in width, which shall have unobstructed access to a public street. Where interior drives are paved to a width of 26 feet or more, the required guest parking area shall be waived. Drives exceeding 20 feet may be required when warranted by proposed traffic.
(3) Walkways not less than three feet wide shall be provided from the mobile home spaces to service buildings and to facilitate safe and convenient pedestrian traffic throughout the park.
(f) Recreation area. Not less than eight percent of the gross site area shall be devoted to recreational facilities, generally provided in a central location. The recreation area shall be designed and developed for active recreation. Where individual lots are substantially above minimum standards and provide for sufficient outdoor recreation, an exemption may be granted to an extent that an absolute minimum of 100 square feet per lot be considered sufficient for the site of a centralized recreation area, provided that no recreation area shall contain less than 5,000 square feet.
(g) Water and sewage. Each mobile home space shall be provided with and each mobile home shall be connected to a central sanitary sewerage and water supply system approved by the health authority and the plumbing inspector.
(h) Lighting and overhead wires.
(1) All wiring shall be underground. Adequate lighting shall be provided to illuminate streets, drives, and walks for safe movement of vehicles and pedestrians at night. To provide exterior lighting for mobile home parks, the following standards are required:
a. Discharge-type luminaries not smaller than 7,000 lumens shall be used. (Incandescent lamps are not acceptable.)
b. All street intersections shall be lighted.
c. Pole placement and luminaire mounting shall be planned to get maximum utilization of light on street areas.
(2) The preferred mounting height for roadway luminaries is 27 feet for 7,000 lumens and 30 feet for 20,000 lumens. The minimum mounting height for a post top luminaire is 16 feet. The minimum mounting height shall be 15 feet. Mounting heights are measured from ground level to bottom of luminaire.
(3) The ratio of average to minimum street illumination (footcandles) shall not exceed six to one. The illumination ratio shall be determined by using IES (Illuminating Engineering Society) calculation methods and luminaire manufacturer's standard performance data. The average horizontal footcandles should be not less than two-tenths. This will result in 7,000 lumen roadway type luminaries mounted approximately 27 feet above ground and spaced 200 to 250 feet. (The exact spacing will depend on the luminaire selected.)
(i) Refuse disposal.
(1) Every mobile home lot shall be provided with at least one 20-gallon garbage can, of acceptable material with a tightfitting cover. The cans shall be kept in a sanitary condition at all times. It shall be the responsibility of the park owner to insure that garbage and rubbish shall be collected and properly disposed of. Collection shall be at least twice weekly.
(2) Stands in which the garbage cans can be placed shall also be provided and so designed as to prevent containers from being tipped, to minimize spillage and container deterioration, and to facilitate cleaning around them.
(j) Service building. Every mobile home park not in existence, licensed and in operation on the effective date of this section shall be provided with a service building containing emergency sanitary facilities consisting of at least one lavatory with hot and cold water and one flush toilet for each sex per 100 mobile home lots or fraction thereof. The building containing such emergency sanitary facilities shall be accessible to all mobile homes and may be provided in connection with laundry and other service facilities. The design for the service building shall be submitted as part of the application for permit.
(k) Signing. Each mobile home park shall be permitted to display on each street frontage one identifying sign of a maximum size of nine square feet. The sign shall contain thereon only the name and address of the mobile home park and may only be lighted by indirect lighting.

1427:
(a) Responsibilities of management.
(1) The person to whom a license for a mobile home park is issued shall provide adequate supervision to maintain the park in compliance with this chapter and to keep its facilities and equipment in good repair and in a clean and sanitary condition.
(2) The management is charged with the responsibility of informing the residents of all applicable provisions of this chapter and of their duties and responsibilities under this chapter. A copy of section 23-138 shall be displayed in the mobile home park.
(3) The management shall supervise the placement of each mobile home on its mobile home stand, which includes securing its stability and installing all utility connections.
(4) The management shall maintain a register containing the names of all park residents identified by lot number or street address and shall show each change in lot occupancy. Such register shall be available to any authorized person inspecting the park.
(b) Responsibilities of residents.
(1) The resident shall comply with all applicable requirements of this chapter and shall maintain his mobile home lot, its facilities, and equipment in good repair and in clean and sanitary condition.
(2) The open area under a mobile home shall be totally enclosed by skirting constructed of suitable weatherproof material.
(3) No flammable mixtures will be stored under the mobile home. Stored items shall be located so as not to interfere with the underneath inspection of the mobile home.
(4) First aid fire extinguishers for class B and class C fires shall be kept at the premises and maintained in working condition. All fire extinguishers shall be subject to inspection by an authorized official.
(c) Accessory structures.
(1) Accessory structures shall be designed in a manner that will enhance the appearance of the mobile home park.
(2) Only one accessory structure will be allowed on each lot. A building permit will be required for each such structure as construction and electrical installation will be subject to existing city codes. Electrical circuits supplying the accessory structure shall be independent of the circuit supplying the mobile home. All setback requirements shall be maintained.
(d) Mobile home placement and anchorage. The mobile home shall be properly secured against high wind velocity. Overturning, sliding, or uplift shall be prevented through anchors, tie-downs, or similar devices acceptable to the building inspection department.
(e) Insect and rodent control.
(1) Grounds, buildings, and structures shall be maintained free of insects and rodent harborage and infestation. Examination methods and other methods to control insects and rodents shall conform with the requirements of the health department.
(2) Storage shall be so maintained as to prevent rodent harborage. Lumber, pipes and other building materials shall be stored at least one foot above the ground.
(Code 1981, § 8-6062)
Cross reference— Animals, ch. 4; fire prevention and protection, ch. 9.
1428:
(a) Existing mobile home parks.
(1) All existing mobile home parks in the city which do not comply with regulations contained in this chapter shall be permitted one year to be brought into conformance.
(2) Should any existing mobile home park not be able to comply with the criteria for an R-3 zone, it will remain in nonconformance but must meet all other health and safety factors of this chapter. Prior to receiving a license, an itemized schedule will be provided each applicant, indicating deficiencies to be corrected.
(b) Mobile homes on individual lots. From and after the adoption of this chapter no mobile home shall be placed on an individual lot outside an R-3 zone for residential purposes.
